transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The 4C code on Samsung washing machines typically means there is a problem with the water supply—specifically that not enough water is entering the machine within the expected time. Before you call an engineer, this is often caused by something simple like a blocked inlet filter or a kinked hose. 1. Ensure the tap behind the machine is turned fully on and the fill hose isn't kinked against the wall.
2. Turn off the tap, unscrew the fill hose from the back of the machine, and check the small mesh filter inside the inlet for grit or scale blockage. If you find it blocked, clean it under a tap and try again.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]

Tap was already open, and I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway, no change. Hose isn't kinked. I unscrewed the hose and the mesh filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. I've cleaned it, refitted it and run it again: it fills normally now and the 4C has gone.

That’s excellent news. It was most likely the grit and limescale blocking that inlet filter, which is a very common cause for the 4C code on Samsung machines. If it happens frequently in your area, you might also consider installing a whole-house water filter. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

claimsRejected.claim: If the filter is already clean and the tap/hose are fine, please let me know what you found.

candidates: Blocked inlet mesh filter or kinked hose (high)
Tap not fully open or low water pressure (medium)

reading.symptom: error code appears after a couple of minutes, drum is dry

plan: They asked: "Any ideas before I call someone out?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Samsung; model WW90T534DAW; code 4C.
The fault they reported is: "error code appears after a couple of minutes, drum is dry". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

plan: The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

checked hose for kinks: hose isn't kinked
unscrewed hose and checked mesh filter: filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits
